title: Sir Geoffrey Wilkinson Lecture 2026 – Towards Solar Fuels and Fertilisers
desc:
Towards Solar Fuels and Fertilisers: Managing Proton and Electron Currency through Molecular Design

Life runs on electrons and protons. Together, or as hydrogen-atom equivalents, they allow plants to store solar energy, underpin the fuels that power society, and help make the fertilisers needed to sustain life.

Simply put, hydrogen atoms decorate many of the key molecular building blocks of our world. Chemists would like to harness this same basic currency to make fuels, fertilisers, and other useful molecules using renewable electricity or light.

The challenge is control. Protons and electrons readily combine to make hydrogen gas, often more easily than they can be directed toward other molecules. Learning how to steer them selectively is therefore a central problem in modern…

title: GATP Seminar – Du Pei (SDU Denmark)
desc: In this talk, I will outline an approach to studying skein modules of 3-manifolds by embedding them into the Hilbert spaces of four-dimensional supersymmetric gauge theories. When the 3-manifold has reduced holonomy, this approach leads to an algorithm for the dimension of the skein module for a general gauge group, expressed as a sum over nilpotent orbits. Surprisingly, the dimensions obtained in this way often differ between Langlands-dual pairs.

title: Dynamical Systems Seminar – Ian Morris (Queen Mary University of London)
desc:
Speaker : Ian Morris

Title : Stability of linear switched systems under periodic inputs

Abstract : Consider a pair of matrices A and B acting on R^d. At each time n we apply either the matrix A or the matrix B, according to some predetermined sequence called the switching law. We would like to know whether or not every trajectory of the resulting system converges to the origin. A landmark result of Bousch and Mairesse in 2002 showed that if the system is stable for all periodic switching laws, it does not follow that it is stable for arbitrary switching laws. In this talk I will discuss continuous-time analogues of this problem, showing that stability with respect to periodic switching laws implies stability under arbitrary switching laws precisely when d \leq 3. This is joint work…

title: Finance and Stochastics Seminar – Mao Fabrice Djete
desc:
Speaker : Mao Fabrice Djete

Title : A New Notion of BSDE for Measure-Dependent Control Problems and Its Applications

Abstract : I will introduce a notion of backward stochastic differential equation (BSDE) for optimization problems with measure dependence. I will begin with two examples that illustrate why a new formulation is needed: a “robust” principal–agent problem and a mean-field optimal stopping problem. I will then develop the BSDE formulation in the Markovian setting before turning to the non-Markovian case. Finally, I will discuss what well-posedness of these equations tells us about the underlying control problems, highlighting settings in which the approach works under weaker assumptions than existing methods or applies where standard techniques are not available.

title: Astrophysics Weekly Seminar: Steven Rendon Restrepo – Exploring Gravitational Instability in 2D simulations and the nature of stochastic fragmentation
desc: Gravitational instability (GI) is a key physical process in which a disc becomes unstable to its own gravity, driving outward angular momentum transport, mass accretion onto the central star, and even the amplification of magnetic fields through a dynamo effect. Most importantly, it is a leading theory of planet formation, describing how a disc can fragment into bound clumps when cooling is efficient. Most simulations characterising GI have relied on a thin-disc (2D) approximation, employing either a zero or a finite smoothing length for the self-gravity potential. A finite smoothing length, however, suppresses the genuinely Newtonian nature of gravity and violates Newton’s third law, potentially inhibiting gravitational collapse. desc:
Prof Ed Bueler (University of Alaska Fairbanks) : The mathematical (and numerical) problem of glaciation

Lectures will be held on Tuesdays: 20 Oct, 27 Oct, 3 Nov, 17 Nov, at 15:00.

Abstract: This four-lecture series introduces variational inequalities to a general applied mathematical audience, pursues their finite element solution, and applies them to a geophysical problem.
